lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Paul writes from prison to the church at Philippi about joy, the humility of Christ, pressing toward the goal, and contentment (1:1-4:23).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of Philippians and say what Paul says about joy?
ev: Say where Paul was when he wrote (1:7, 1:13)
Name the theme that recurs, rejoicing (e.g. 3:1, 4:4)

nodes.t: Thanksgiving and prayer for the Philippians
nodes.d: Paul thanks God for the Philippians' partnership in the gospel, is confident that God will complete the good work begun in them, and prays that their love will grow in knowledge and they be filled with the fruits of righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul is confident that God will do, using Philippians 1:6?
ev: Quote the confidence of 1:6
Say what Paul prays for in 1:9-11

nodes.t: Paul in chains: Christ is preached
nodes.d: Paul says his imprisonment has advanced the gospel, that Christ is preached whether from envy or love, and that he rejoices in this.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul rejoices in prison, using Philippians 1:12-18?
ev: Say what happened because of Paul's bonds (1:12-14)
Contrast the two kinds of preachers (1:15-17)

nodes.t: To live is Christ, to die is gain
nodes.d: Paul says Christ will be magnified in his body whether by life or death, that to live is Christ and to die is gain, and urges the Philippians to live worthy of the gospel, standing firm together and not afraid of opponents.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by "to live is Christ, and to die is gain" in Philippians 1:21?
ev: Quote 1:21
Explain Paul's dilemma (1:22-25)
Say what Paul asks of the Philippians (1:27-28)
Say what has been granted to them (1:29)

nodes.t: The mind of Christ: humbled and exalted
nodes.d: Paul urges unity and humility, pointing to Christ, who being in the form of God took the form of a servant, humbled himself to death on a cross, and was highly exalted so that every knee will bow and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the path of Christ in Philippians 2:6-11 and say how it applies to us in 2:3-5?
ev: Describe the steps of Christ's humbling (2:6-8)
Say what God did in response (2:9-11)
Say what attitude Paul asks of the Philippians (2:3-5)

nodes.t: Work out your salvation: shining as lights
nodes.d: Paul tells the Philippians to work out their own salvation with fear and trembling because God works in them, to do all things without grumbling, and to shine as lights holding forth the word of life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says "work out your own salvation" and then adds that God works in you (Philippians 2:12-13)?
ev: Explain 2:12-13 together
Say what the Philippians are to do among a crooked generation (2:14-16)

nodes.d: Paul commends Timothy, who cares for the Philippians like a son serving with his father, and Epaphroditus, who nearly died serving the work of Christ and whom Paul sends back to them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about Timothy and Epaphroditus in Philippians 2:19-30?
ev: Say what Paul says of Timothy (2:20-22)
Describe what happened to Epaphroditus (2:25-30)

nodes.t: Counting all things loss for Christ
nodes.d: Paul warns against those who trust the flesh, lists his own credentials, and says he counts them loss for the knowledge of Christ, wanting the righteousness that comes through faith in Christ rather than his own righteousness from the law.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul gave up and what he gained, using Philippians 3:7-9?
ev: List Paul's credentials (3:5-6)
State what Paul wants instead (3:8-10)
Explain which righteousness Paul wants (3:9)

nodes.t: Pressing toward the goal and our citizenship in heaven
nodes.d: Paul says he has not yet attained but presses toward the prize of the upward call, urges the Philippians to follow his example and not live as enemies of the cross, and says our citizenship is in heaven, from where we await the Saviour who will transform our bodies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Paul's "one thing I do" in Philippians 3:13-14 and what believers await in 3:20-21?
ev: Describe what Paul does (3:13-14)
Contrast the enemies of the cross with believers (3:18-20)
Say what the Saviour will do (3:21)

nodes.t: Rejoice, do not be anxious, think on these things
nodes.d: Paul urges unity between two women, tells the Philippians to rejoice in the Lord always, to pray with thanksgiving instead of being anxious so that the peace of God guards them, and to think on what is true, honest, just and pure.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says to do instead of being anxious, using Philippians 4:6-7?
ev: Quote the commands of 4:4 and 4:6
Say what the peace of God does (4:7)
List some things to think on (4:8)

nodes.t: Content in every state and God's supply
nodes.d: Paul thanks the Philippians for their gift, says he has learned to be content whether abased or abounding, that he can do all things through Christ who strengthens him, and that God will supply all their need; he closes with greetings.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about contentment in Philippians 4:11-13?
ev: Say what Paul learned (4:11-12)
Quote 4:13 and 4:19
Describe how Paul treats the Philippians' gift (4:17-18)

nodes.d: Isaiah son of Amoz sees visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; the book moves from indictment and judgment to comfort, a servant, and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Isaiah was and describe, using Isaiah 1:1 and 40:1-2, how the book moves from rebuke to comfort?
ev: Name the four kings of Judah named in Isaiah 1:1
Describe the shift in tone between chapters 1-39 and chapter 40 using the texts

nodes.t: Cyrus, the LORD's shepherd and anointed
nodes.d: The LORD names Cyrus, by name before his time, as his shepherd and anointed who will let Jerusalem and the temple be rebuilt, so that all will know there is none else.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says Cyrus will do and why in Isaiah 44:28-45:6?
ev: Say what the LORD says of Cyrus (44:28, 45:1)
Explain why the LORD calls Cyrus by name (45:4-6)
Quote the invitation in 45:22-23
